correctness.rationale: The positive quartic weights sum to one by Vandermonde convolution; the finite-biharmonic Toeplitz block sends them to 6/binom(n+2,5) times the all-ones vector. This gives exact norm, center and interior contact distance. Direct endpoint products give clearance 4-6n/binom(n+2,5), with equality only at n=4. The weighted squared-distance identity proves the global minimum and unique center. The n=3 exceptional case is independently checked with rational barycentric weights. Exact checker reconstructs full Laplacian matrices through n=80 and checks the polynomial identity through n=1000; finite computations supplement the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: Literature-led from Braun–Meyer 2017 and Meyer–Pllaha 2018. Actual semantic published-finding corpus and web searches found tree-Laplacian inradius and path normal-cone work, plus complete-bipartite minimum-ball results. Full available public result texts and relevant primary-paper portions were compared by implication: none evaluates the path minimum enclosing sphere, its quartic support measure or n=5 endpoint screening. Generic simplex minimum-ball optimality is prior mathematics and is credited, not claimed new. Equivalent older graph-Laplacian or biharmonic formulas remain a historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The canonical Euclidean shape of Laplacian simplices is not determined by their unimodular equivalence. A complete, nontrivial all-order minimum-ball classification for the path family identifies a sharp n=4/5 contact transition, a positive discrete biharmonic support distribution, a closed quadratic center and a fifth-order radius deficit. These are natural extremal geometric invariants, rather than a finite recomputation or a gratuitous parameter slice.
